items.title: Iran begins three-day farewell ceremony for Khamenei in Tehran

featured_image.name: Khamenei's death shakes Islamic Republic, Iran switches to ...

items.description:
Iran is holding a three-day public farewell ceremony for Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, the supreme leader killed at age 86 in joint U.S.-Israeli strikes on February 28, with plans to bury him in the holy city of Mashhad, his birthplace.

The ceremony began late Wednesday at Tehran's Imam Khomeini Prayer Hall, according to Reuters, which reported that Hojjatoleslam Mahmoudi, head of Iran's Islamic Propagation Council, invited the public to pay their respects starting at 10 p.m. local time. Details of the funeral procession are to be announced separately. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said on its Telegram account that a "large farewell ceremony" would be held in the capital before the burial.[1][2][3]

items.title: South Korea halts trading as Asian markets plunge on Iran war fears

featured_image.name: South Korea’s stock market in meltdown amid US-Iran war

items.description:
Asian stock markets suffered steep losses on Wednesday as the widening war between the United States, Israel, and Iran sent oil prices climbing higher and rattled investor confidence across the region. South Korea's Kospi plunged as much as 10%, triggering circuit breakers that temporarily halted trading, while Japan's Nikkei 225 fell nearly 4% and Hong Kong's Hang Seng dropped 2.8%.[1]

The sell-off marks the deepest rout in Asian equities since the U.S. and Israel launched coordinated strikes on Iran late on February 28, killing Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei and sparking retaliatory attacks across the region. President Donald Trump has signaled the military campaign could last weeks.[2][3][4]

items.description: Researchers at Mississippi State University have published a new study showing that snow cover across the Northern Hemisphere is declining, with nearly three times as many regions losing snow as gaining it. items.title: US and Ecuador launch joint military strikes on drug cartels

featured_image.name: Ecuador calls off arms exchange with US over plan to send ...

items.description:
Ecuadorian and U.S. military forces launched joint operations against designated terrorist organizations inside Ecuador on March 3, marking a new front in the South American nation's escalating war against drug cartels. The U.S. Southern Command announced the operations, calling them "a powerful example of the commitment of partners in Latin America and the Caribbean to combat the scourge of" narco-terrorism.[1]

The launch follows a weekend of high-level meetings in Quito, where SOUTHCOM Commander Gen. Francis L. Donovan met with President Daniel Noboa and senior defense officials on March 1-2 to finalize plans for security cooperation. Noboa announced the initiative on X, writing: "In March, we will carry out joint operations alongside our regional allies, including the United States".[2][3][4]

items.title: UN warns El Niño could return later this year

featured_image.name: El Niño is creating an unexpected atmospheric pattern, but ...

items.description:
The World Meteorological Organization warned on Tuesday that El Niño could develop later this year as the current La Niña weakens, a shift that climate scientists say could push global temperatures toward new records in 2027.

The WMO's latest update, issued March 3, forecasts a 60% chance of neutral conditions — neither El Niño nor La Niña — during March through May, rising to 70% during April through June. But the probability of El Niño increases steadily thereafter, reaching roughly 40% by May through July.[1][2]
